gap: No result ChatGPT got states what silence costs per key: Gamakay's Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switches are $13.99 per 45-pack (about $0.31 a switch), so two packs ($27.98) convert any compatible Hall effect board of up to 90 keys, which is 31% of the price of a new $89.99 TK75HE V2.
standout_why: Compared against the hlplanet Hall effect guide (cited), thegadgetverse silent-switch roundup, the mechvibes sound-test page, and the RTINGS quiet list. The hlplanet guide gives the $89.99 board price and calls Phoenix V3 'essentially the only mainstream silent magnetic option', but has no switch price, pack size or swap cost. Thegadgetverse states 'no prices' and no pack size for Phoenix V3, and says no lab has published a numeric noise score for any silent HE switch. Mechvibes has no dB figures or prices. The RTINGS quiet list returned only its navigation shell to my fetcher, so I could not compare against its body text. The per-switch price does appear in hlplanet's separate Phoenix V3 review, which ChatGPT did not retrieve. I found no measured dBA for any candidate, so the derived figure is cost, not loudness.
decides: It splits the answer by what the shopper already owns. Someone with a compatible board (hlplanet's Marcus Richardson tested Phoenix V3 in a Wooting 60HE) gets silent switches for $27.98 instead of buying a new board. Someone buying new has it confirmed that the TK75HE V2 at $89.99 with silent switches fitted costs less than any louder board plus a swap set. It also flags that Gamakay's NS75 is $10 cheaper at $79.99 and hlplanet lists a Phoenix V3 option for it.

findings.product: Gamakay Phoenix V3 silent magnetic switch
findings.label: Force and travel, and the derived trade-off
findings.value: 45 ± 5 gf actuation, 58 gf bottom-out, 3.5 ± 0.2 mm travel; 0.5 mm (12.5%) shorter than the 4.0 mm standard and 10 gf (21%) heavier at bottom-out than Gateron White Jade
findings.source_title: Review: Gamakay Phoenix V3 Silent Magnetic Switch (HLPLANET)
findings.note: 4.0 - 3.5 = 0.5 mm, 0.5 / 4.0 = 12.5%. 58 - 48 = 10 gf, 10 / 48 = 20.8%; White Jade's 48 gf maximum is from hlplanet's comparison table. Magnetic flux is 95 ± 15 Gs initial and 580 ± 50 Gs at bottom. Richardson's noise verdict is 'Really quiet with decent quality', with no dB figure.
